description: Measured behaviour of YouTube's caption-endpoint rate limit, which youtube-transcript-api reports as IpBlocked (HTTP 429). Recorded because the library documents no recovery time and no safe request rate.
endpoint: timedtext caption fetch plus the watch-page player response

IpBlocked: _transcripts.py: watch page returned a g-recaptcha challenge

sessions.outcome: HTTP 429 starting at video 12, despite halving the request rate

findings: The reset time is NOT known. Measurements give bounds only: still blocked 53 minutes after onset, clear 23h40m after onset. Nothing in between was probed.
The earlier figure of ~24 hours was an upper bound from a single observation, not a measured reset time.
Halving the request rate did not help: session A got 74 videos, session B got 10 at roughly half the speed, so the allowance looks cumulative rather than per-window.
One blocked probe costs exactly one video = two HTTP requests (one list, one fetch) and about two seconds. Measured from the run log, not estimated.

Because the reset time is unknown, the scheduled resume probes on an exponential backoff (1h, 2h, 4h, capped at 4h) counted from consecutive blocked probes and restarts when captions arrive. The schedule itself is therefore the instrument that measures the reset time.

operational_consequence.why: Stop at the first 429 instead of grinding through cooldowns, then wait a long interval before the next session.

probe_schedule.restarts_when: a probe returns captions, which proves the window reopened

session_b_log_note: The first four auto-resume rows (18:43:43, 18:44:05, 18:45:13, 18:45:34) were manual test invocations inside a two-minute window, not four independent probes. The live log keeps one row; the rest are preserved in data/expanded/auto-resume-log.full-backup.jsonl.
